content.shloka:
Om Bhur Bhuvah Svah
Tat Savitur Varenyam
Bhargo Devasya Dhimahi
Dhiyo Yo Nah Prachodayat
content.meaning: We meditate upon the divine light of the radiant Sun (Savitur). May that supreme brilliance illuminate our intellect and guide us on the path of righteousness.
content.transliteration:
Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ
Tat Savitūr Vareṇyam
Bhargo Devasya Dhīmahi
Dhiyo Yo Naḥ Prachodayāt

content.shloka:
Om Apo Jyotiraso Amritam Brahma
Bhur Bhuvah Svar Om
content.meaning: Om, the essence of water, light, taste, and immortality is Brahman. The three worlds - earth, atmosphere, and heaven - are all Om.
content.transliteration:
Om Āpo Jyotīraso Amṛtam Brahma
Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svar Om

content.shloka:
Aya Atu Varada Devi
Aksharam Brahmasammitam
Gayatrim Chandasam Mata
Idam Brahma Jushashva Nah
content.meaning: O boon-giving Goddess, come to us. You are the imperishable one, equal to Brahman. O Gayatri, mother of all Vedic metres, accept our offerings and bless us.
content.transliteration:
Āyā Ātu Varadā Devī
Akṣaraṁ Brahmasaṁmitam
Gāyatrīṁ Chandasāṁ Mātā
Idaṁ Brahma Juṣasva Naḥ

content.shloka:
Ojosi Sahosi Balamasi
Bhrajosi Devanam Dhama Namasi
Vishvamasi Vishvayuh Sarvamasi
Sarvayuh Abhibhuh Om
content.meaning: You are vigor, you are endurance, you are strength. You are brilliance, the abode of the gods. You are the universe, the life of the universe. You are everything, the life of all. You are the supreme ruler. Om.
content.transliteration:
Ojosi Sahosi Balamasi
Bhrājosi Devānāṁ Dhāma Nāmasi
Viśvamasi Viśvāyuḥ Sarvamasi
Sarvāyuḥ Abhibhūḥ Om

content.shloka:
Mukta Vidruma Hema Nila
Dhavala Chchayair Mukha Tristhaneya
Trinetram Cha Yuktam Indu Shakalam
Maulim Hamsasthaam Smaraami Gayatrim
content.meaning: I meditate upon Goddess Gayatri who has five faces of the colors of pearl, coral, gold, blue, and white, who has three eyes, who wears the crescent moon on her crown, and who is seated upon a swan.
content.transliteration:
Muktā Vidruma Hema Nīla
Dhavala Cchāyair Mukhā Tristhāneyā
Trinetrāṁ Cha Yuktam Indu Śakalaṁ
Maulim Haṁsasthāṁ Smarāmi Gāyatrīm

content.shloka:
Gayatrim Chandasam Mata
Idam Brahma Jushashva Me
Yadahnat Kurute Papam
Tadahnat Pratimuchyate
content.meaning: O Gayatri, mother of all Vedic metres, bless me with the knowledge of Brahman. Whatever sins are committed during the day are destroyed by the recitation of the Gayatri Mantra at dusk.
content.transliteration:
Gāyatrīṁ Chandasāṁ Mātā
Idaṁ Brahma Juṣasva Me
Yadahnāt Kurute Pāpaṁ
Tadahnāt Pratimuchyate

content.shloka:
Om Tryambakam Yajamahe
Sugandhim Pushtivardhanam
Urvarukamiva Bandhanan
Mrityormukshiya Mamritat
content.meaning: We worship the three-eyed Lord Shiva, who is fragrant and nourishes all beings. May He liberate us from the bondage of death, just as a ripe cucumber is severed from its vine. May He grant us immortality.
content.transliteration:
Om Tryambakaṁ Yajāmahe
Sugandhiṁ Puṣṭivardhanam
Urvārukamiva Bandhanān
Mṛtyormukṣīya Māmṛtāt

content.shloka:
Om Haum Joom Sah
Bhur Bhuvah Svah
Om Tryambakam Yajamahe
Sugandhim Pushtivardhanam
Urvarukamiva Bandhanan
Mrityormukshiya Mamritat
Svah Bhuvah Bhuh Om
Sah Joom Haum Om
content.meaning: This is the extended Mahamrityunjaya Mantra with the beeja (seed) mantras. The seed syllables Haum, Joom, and Sah invoke Lord Shiva's protective energy. The three worlds are invoked, and the core mantra is enclosed within these sacred syllables for enhanced spiritual power.
content.transliteration:
Om Hauṁ Jūṁ Saḥ
Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ
Om Tryambakaṁ Yajāmahe
Sugandhiṁ Puṣṭivardhanam
Urvārukamiva Bandhanān
Mṛtyormukṣīya Māmṛtāt
Svaḥ Bhuvaḥ Bhūḥ Om
Saḥ Jūṁ Hauṁ Om

content.shloka:
Dhyayet Satatam Mahesham
Rajata Giri Nibham Charu Chandravatamsam
Ratnakalpojjvalingam Parashu Mrigavarabhi
Ti Prashastam Prasannam
content.meaning: One should always meditate upon Lord Maheshvara (Shiva), who shines like a silver mountain, who is adorned with the beautiful crescent moon, who is radiant with jeweled ornaments, who holds an axe and a deer in his hands, and who is ever gracious.
content.transliteration:
Dhyāyet Satataṁ Maheśaṁ
Rajata Giri Nibhaṁ Chāru Chandrāvatamsam
Ratnākalpojjvaliṅgaṁ Paraśu Mṛgavarābhī
Ti Praśāstaṁ Prasannam

content.shloka:
Karpur Gauram Karunavataram
Sansara Saram Bhujagendra Haram
Sada Vasantam Hridayaravinde
Bhavam Bhavani Sahitam Namami
content.meaning: I bow to Lord Shiva who is white as camphor, the incarnation of compassion, the essence of the world, who wears the king of serpents as a garland, who always dwells in the lotus of the heart, and who is accompanied by Goddess Bhavani (Parvati).
content.transliteration:
Karpūra Gauraṁ Karuṇāvatāraṁ
Saṁsāra Sāraṁ Bhujagendrā Hāram
Sadā Vasantaṁ Hṛdayāravinde
Bhavaṁ Bhavānī Sahitaṁ Namāmi

content.shloka:
Mahamrityunjaya Mantra Japa
Samarpayami
Anena Japena Shri Mrityunjaya
Devata Priyatam
content.meaning: I offer the fruits of this Mahamrityunjaya Mantra recitation. May Lord Mrityunjaya (the conqueror of death) be pleased with this chanting. This is the traditional concluding prayer recited after completing the japa (repetition) of the mantra.
content.transliteration:
Mahāmṛtyuñjaya Mantra Japa
Samarpayāmi
Anena Japena Śrī Mṛtyuñjaya
Devatā Prīyatām

content.shloka: Om Gam Ganapataye Namah
content.meaning: Salutations to Lord Ganesha, the remover of all obstacles. 'Gam' is the seed syllable of Ganesha. By chanting this mantra, one invokes the blessings of Lord Ganesha for success in all undertakings.
content.transliteration: Om Gaṁ Gaṇapataye Namaḥ

content.shloka:
Vakratunda Mahakaya
Suryakoti Samaprabha
Nirvighnam Kuru Me Deva
Sarva Karyeshu Sarvada
content.meaning: O Lord with the curved trunk and massive body, whose splendor is equal to a billion suns, please remove all obstacles from my endeavors, always and in all my tasks.
content.transliteration:
Vakratuṇḍa Mahākāya
Sūryakoṭi Samaprabha
Nirvighnaṁ Kuru Me Deva
Sarva Kāryeṣu Sarvadā

content.shloka:
Ekadantam Mahakayam
Taptakanchana Sannibham
Lambodaram Vishaladaksham
Vandeyam Ganananayakam
content.meaning: I bow to the leader of the ganas (celestial attendants) who has one tusk, a massive form, who shines like molten gold, who has a large belly and broad eyes.
content.transliteration:
Ekadantaṁ Mahākāyaṁ
Taptakāñchana Sannibham
Lambodaraṁ Viśālākṣaṁ
Vandehaṁ Gaṇanāyakam

content.shloka:
Gajaananam Bhuta Ganadi Sevitam
Kapittha Jambu Phala Sara Bhakshitam
Umasutam Shoka Vinasha Karanam
Namami Vigneshvara Pada Pankajam
content.meaning: I bow at the lotus feet of Lord Vigneshvara (remover of obstacles), who has an elephant face, who is served by the host of celestial beings, who eats the essence of kapitha and jambu fruits, who is the son of Uma (Parvati), and who destroys all sorrows.
content.transliteration:
Gajānanaṁ Bhūta Gaṇādi Sevitaṁ
Kapittha Jambū Phala Sāra Bhakṣitam
Umāsutaṁ Śoka Vināśa Kāraṇaṁ
Namāmi Vighneśvara Pāda Paṅkajam

content.shloka:
Om Shri Ganeshaya Namah
Sumukhashchaikadantashcha
Kapilo Gajakarnakah
Lambodarashcha Vikato
Vighnanasho Ganadhipah
content.meaning: Salutations to Lord Ganesha. He who has a beautiful face, he who has one tusk, he who is tawny-colored, he who has elephant ears, he who has a large belly, he who is extraordinary, he who destroys obstacles, and he who is the lord of the ganas.
content.transliteration:
Om Śrī Gaṇeśāya Namaḥ
Sumukhāścaikadantaśca
Kapilo Gajakarṇakaḥ
Lambodaraśca Vikaṭo
Vighnanāśo Gaṇādhipaḥ

content.shloka:
Agajanana Padmarkam
Gajanana Maharnisham
Aneka Dantam Bhaktanam
Eka Dantam Upasmahe
content.meaning: We meditate upon the one-tusked Lord who is like the lotus born from the mountain (Parvati), who has the face of an elephant, who is worshipped day and night, and who grants many boons to his devotees.
content.transliteration:
Agajānana Padmārkaṁ
Gajānana Maharniśam
Aneka Dantaṁ Bhaktānāṁ
Eka Dantam Upāsmahe

content.shloka: Om Aim Saraswatyai Namah
content.meaning: Salutations to Goddess Saraswati. 'Aim' is the beeja (seed) mantra of Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge, wisdom, arts, and learning. Chanting this mantra invokes her blessings for intellectual growth and creative expression.
content.transliteration: Om Aiṁ Sarasvatyai Namaḥ

content.shloka:
Saraswati Namastubhyam
Varade Kamarupini
Vidyarambham Karishyami
Siddhir Bhavatu Me Sada
content.meaning: O Goddess Saraswati, salutations to you, the giver of boons and the fulfiller of desires. I am beginning my studies; may I always attain success in my learning.
content.transliteration:
Sarasvatī Namastubhyaṁ
Varade Kāmarūpiṇī
Vidyārambhaṁ Kariṣyāmi
Siddhir Bhavatu Me Sadā

content.shloka:
Ya Kundendu Tushara Hara Dhavala
Ya Shubhra Vastravrita
Ya Veena Varadanda Manditakara
Ya Shveta Padmasana
Ya Brahmachyuta Shankara Prabhritibhir
Devaih Sada Pujita
Sa Mam Patu Saraswati Bhagavati
Nishshesha Jadyapaha
content.meaning: May Goddess Saraswati protect me - she who is as white as the jasmine flower, the moon, and the frost; who is dressed in pure white garments; whose hands are adorned with the veena and the gesture of blessing; who is seated on a white lotus; who is always worshipped by Brahma, Vishnu, Shankara, and other gods; and who removes all forms of ignorance.
content.transliteration:
Yā Kundendu Tuṣāra Hāra Dhavalā
Yā Śubhra Vastrāvṛtā
Yā Vīṇā Varadaṇḍa Maṇḍitakarā
Yā Śveta Padmāsanā
Yā Brahmāchyuta Śaṅkara Prabhṛtibhir
Devaiḥ Sadā Pūjitā
Sā Māṁ Pātu Sarasvatī Bhagavatī
Niḥśeṣa Jāḍyāpahā

content.shloka:
Shuklam Brahmavichara Sara
Paramam Adyam Jagadvyapinim
Veena Pustaka Dharineem Abhayadam
Jadyandhakarapaha
Haste Sphatikamalikam Vidadhatim
Padmasane Samsthitam
Vande Tam Parameshvarim Bhagavatim
Buddhipradam Sharadam
content.meaning: I worship that supreme Goddess Sharada (Saraswati), who is dressed in white, who embodies the essence of Brahman knowledge, who pervades the entire universe, who holds the veena and book, who dispels the darkness of ignorance, who holds a crystal rosary, who is seated on the lotus, and who bestows intelligence.
content.transliteration:
Śuklāṁ Brahmavichāra Sāra
Paramām Ādyāṁ Jagadvyāpinīṁ
Vīṇā Pustaka Dhāriṇīṁ Abhayadāṁ
Jāḍyāndhakārāpahā
Haste Sphaṭikamālikāṁ Vidadhatīṁ
Padmāsane Saṁsthitām
Vande Tāṁ Parameśvarīṁ Bhagavatīṁ
Buddhipradāṁ Śāradām

content.shloka:
Mahasaraswati Vidhmahe
Mahatapasey Cha Dhimahi
Tanno Saraswati Prachodayat
content.meaning: We know the great Saraswati, we meditate upon the one who performs great penance. May Goddess Saraswati illuminate and inspire our minds. This is the Saraswati Gayatri mantra.
content.transliteration:
Mahāsarasvatī Vidmahe
Mahātapasey Cha Dhīmahi
Tanno Sarasvatī Prachodayāt

content.shloka: Om Namo Narayanaya
content.meaning: Salutations to Lord Narayana (Vishnu). This is the sacred eight-syllable mantra (Ashtakshara) dedicated to Lord Vishnu, the preserver of the universe. It signifies complete surrender to the Supreme Lord.
content.transliteration: Om Namo Nārāyaṇāya

content.shloka: Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya
content.meaning: Salutations to Lord Vasudeva (Krishna, the son of Vasudeva). This twelve-syllable mantra (Dvadasakshari) is one of the most powerful Vishnu mantras, invoking the all-pervading Supreme Being who dwells in all creatures.
content.transliteration: Om Namo Bhagavate Vāsudevāya

content.shloka:
Shantakaram Bhujagashayanam
Padmanabham Suresham
Vishvadharam Gaganasadrisham
Meghavarnam Shubhangam
Lakshmi Kantam Kamalanayanam
Yogirbhih Dhyana Gamyam
Vande Vishnum Bhava Bhaya Haram
Sarva Lokaika Natham
content.meaning: I bow to Lord Vishnu, the embodiment of peace, who reclines on the great serpent Shesha, from whose navel the lotus springs, who is the lord of the gods, who sustains the universe, who is vast as the sky, whose complexion is like the clouds, whose body is auspicious, who is the beloved of Lakshmi, whose eyes are like lotuses, who is accessible through meditation by yogis, who destroys the fear of worldly existence, and who is the sole lord of all worlds.
content.transliteration:
Śāntākāraṁ Bhujagaśayanaṁ
Padmanābhaṁ Sureśam
Viśvādhāraṁ Gaganasadṛśaṁ
Meghavarṇaṁ Śubhāṅgam
Lakṣmī Kāntaṁ Kamalanayanam
Yogirbhiḥ Dhyāna Gamyam
Vande Viṣṇuṁ Bhava Bhaya Haraṁ
Sarva Lokaika Nātham

content.shloka:
Mangalam Bhagavan Vishnuh
Mangalam Garudadhvajah
Mangalam Pundari Kakshah
Mangalaya Tano Harih
content.meaning: Auspiciousness unto Lord Vishnu, auspiciousness unto the one who has Garuda as His banner, auspiciousness unto the one who has lotus-like eyes. May Lord Hari (Vishnu) bring auspiciousness to all.
content.transliteration:
Maṅgalaṁ Bhagavān Viṣṇuḥ
Maṅgalaṁ Garuḍadhvajaḥ
Maṅgalaṁ Puṇḍarī Kākṣaḥ
Maṅgalāya Tano Hariḥ

content.shloka:
Kayena Vacha Manasendriyairva
Buddhyatmanava Prakriteh Svabhavat
Karomi Yadyat Sakalam Parasmai
Narayanayeti Samarpayami
content.meaning: Whatever I do with my body, speech, mind, senses, intellect, soul, or through my natural tendencies - I offer all of it to Lord Narayana. This is the mantra of complete surrender (Samarpanam).
content.transliteration:
Kāyena Vāchā Manasendriyairvā
Buddhyātmanāvā Prakṛteḥ Svabhāvāt
Karomi Yadyat Sakalaṁ Parasmai
Nārāyaṇāyeti Samarpayāmi

content.shloka: Om Dum Durgayei Namah
content.meaning: Salutations to Goddess Durga. 'Dum' is the beeja (seed) mantra of Durga, the invincible one. This mantra invokes the protective and empowering energy of the Divine Mother who vanquishes all evil forces.
content.transliteration: Om Duṁ Durgāyei Namaḥ

content.shloka:
Sarva Mangala Mangalye
Shive Sarvartha Sadhike
Sharanye Tryambake Gauri
Narayani Namostute
content.meaning: O auspicious of all that is auspicious, O consort of Lord Shiva, O one who fulfills all purposes, O the one who provides refuge, O three-eyed Goddess Gauri, O Narayani, I bow to you again and again.
content.transliteration:
Sarva Maṅgala Māṅgalye
Śive Sarvārtha Sādhike
Śaraṇye Tryambake Gaurī
Nārāyaṇi Namostute

content.shloka:
Ya Devi Sarva Bhuteshu
Matri Rupena Samsthita
Ya Devi Sarva Bhuteshu
Shakti Rupena Samsthita
Ya Devi Sarva Bhuteshu
Shanti Rupena Samsthita
Namastasyai Namastasyai
Namastasyai Namo Namah
content.meaning: To the Goddess who resides in all beings in the form of Mother, to the Goddess who resides in all beings in the form of Power, to the Goddess who resides in all beings in the form of Peace - salutations to Her, salutations to Her, salutations to Her, again and again.
content.transliteration:
Yā Devī Sarva Bhūteṣu
Mātṛ Rūpeṇa Saṁsthitā
Yā Devī Sarva Bhūteṣu
Śakti Rūpeṇa Saṁsthitā
Yā Devī Sarva Bhūteṣu
Śānti Rūpeṇa Saṁsthitā
Namastasyai Namastasyai
Namastasyai Namo Namaḥ

content.shloka:
Jatavedasamina Vahanoha
Magnim Durgani Vishva
Sindhum Duritaty Agnih
Parvaktara Hamartyat
content.meaning: I invoke the fire of awareness, Jatavedas (the all-knowing fire). May Goddess Durga, like a ship, carry us across all difficulties and dangers in life, just as fire burns away all impurities.
content.transliteration:
Jātavedasamīnā Vāhanoha
Magniṁ Durgāṇi Viśvā
Sindhuṁ Duritatyāgniḥ
Parvaktārā Hamārtyāt

content.shloka:
Om Jaya Jaya Mahi Surasura Pujite
Sarvasiddhi Dayini Kale
Kala Ratri Mahadevi
Durgadevi Namostute
content.meaning: Glory, glory to the great Goddess who is worshipped by both gods and demons. O giver of all spiritual powers, O Goddess of the dark night, O Great Goddess Durga, I bow to you with reverence.
content.transliteration:
Om Jaya Jaya Mahī Surāsura Pūjite
Sarvasiddhi Dāyinī Kāle
Kāla Rātrī Mahādevī
Durgādevī Namostute

content.shloka:
Srishti Sthiti Vinashanam
Shaktibhute Sanatani
Gunashraye Gunamaye
Narayani Namostute
content.meaning: O eternal Goddess who is the power behind creation, preservation, and destruction, who is the refuge of the three qualities (gunas) and who is the embodiment of these qualities, O Narayani, salutations to you.
content.transliteration:
Sṛṣṭi Sthiti Vināśānāṁ
Śaktibhūte Sanātanī
Guṇāśraye Guṇamaye
Nārāyaṇi Namostute

content.shloka: Om Shreem Mahalakshmiyei Namah
content.meaning: Salutations to the great Goddess Lakshmi. 'Shreem' is the beeja (seed) mantra of Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, prosperity, fortune, and abundance. Chanting this mantra invokes her divine grace for material and spiritual prosperity.
content.transliteration: Om Śrīṁ Mahālakṣmyai Namaḥ

content.shloka:
Namastestu Mahamaye
Shripithe Surapujite
Shankha Chakra Gadahaste
Mahalakshmi Namostute
content.meaning: Salutations to the Great Goddess of Illusion, who resides in the abode of Sri, who is worshipped by the gods, who holds the conch, discus, and mace in her hands. O Mahalakshmi, I bow to you.
content.transliteration:
Namastestu Mahāmāye
Śrīpīṭhe Surapūjite
Śaṅkha Chakra Gadāhaste
Mahālakṣmi Namostute

content.shloka:
Sarvajne Sarvavarade
Sarvadushtabhayankari
Sarva Duhkha Hare Devi
Mahalakshmi Namostute
content.meaning: O all-knowing Goddess, O grantor of all boons, O one who strikes fear in the wicked, O Goddess who removes all sorrows, O Mahalakshmi, I bow to you with reverence.
content.transliteration:
Sarvajñe Sarvavarade
Sarvaduṣṭabhayaṅkarī
Sarva Duḥkha Hare Devī
Mahālakṣmi Namostute

content.shloka:
Siddhi Buddhi Prade Devi
Bhukti Mukti Pradayini
Mantra Murte Sada Devi
Mahalakshmi Namostute
content.meaning: O Goddess who bestows spiritual attainment and wisdom, O giver of worldly enjoyment and liberation, O Goddess who is the embodiment of mantras, O Mahalakshmi, I bow to you always.
content.transliteration:
Siddhi Buddhi Prade Devī
Bhukti Mukti Pradāyinī
Mantra Mūrte Sadā Devī
Mahālakṣmi Namostute

content.shloka:
Padmanane Padmauroo
Padmakshi Padmasambhave
Tanme Bhajasi Padmakshi
Yena Sokhyam Labhamyaham
content.meaning: O one with a lotus face, lotus thighs, lotus eyes, and born from the lotus. O lotus-eyed Goddess, please bless me so that I may attain eternal happiness and well-being.
content.transliteration:
Padmānane Padmaūroo
Padmākṣi Padmasambhave
Tanme Bhajasi Padmākṣī
Yena Saukhyaṁ Labhāmyaham

content.shloka:
Mahalakshmi Cha Vidmahe
Vishnu Patnyai Cha Dhimahi
Tanno Lakshmih Prachodayat
content.meaning: We know the great Lakshmi, we meditate upon the consort of Lord Vishnu. May Goddess Lakshmi illuminate and inspire our minds. This is the Lakshmi Gayatri mantra for invoking prosperity.
content.transliteration:
Mahālakṣmī Cha Vidmahe
Viṣṇu Patnyai Cha Dhīmahi
Tanno Lakṣmīḥ Prachodayāt

content.shloka: Om Ham Hanumate Namah
content.meaning: Salutations to Lord Hanuman. 'Ham' is the beeja (seed) mantra of Hanuman. This mantra invokes the immense strength, devotion, courage, and selfless service embodied by Lord Hanuman, the greatest devotee of Lord Rama.
content.transliteration: Om Haṁ Hanumate Namaḥ

content.shloka:
Manojavam Marutatulyavegam
Jitendriyam Buddhimatam Varishtham
Vatatmajam Vanarayuthamukhyam
Shri Ramadutam Sharanam Prapadye
content.meaning: I take refuge in Lord Hanuman, who is swift as the mind, who equals the wind god in speed, who is the master of the senses, who is foremost among the intelligent, who is the son of the wind god, who is the chief among the monkey warriors, and who is the messenger of Lord Rama.
content.transliteration:
Manojavaṁ Mārutatulyavegaṁ
Jitendriyaṁ Buddhimatāṁ Variṣṭham
Vātātmajaṁ Vānarayūthamukhyaṁ
Śrī Rāmadūtaṁ Śaraṇaṁ Prapadye

content.shloka:
Buddhi Heen Tanu Janike
Sumirau Pavan Kumar
Bal Buddhi Vidya Dehu Mohi
Harahu Kalesh Vikar
content.meaning: Knowing myself to be devoid of intelligence and strength, I remember you, O son of the Wind God. Please grant me strength, intelligence, and knowledge, and remove all my afflictions and impurities.
content.transliteration:
Buddhi Hīn Tanu Jānike
Sumirau Pavan Kumār
Bal Buddhi Vidyā Dehu Mohi
Harahu Kaleś Vikār

content.shloka:
Atul Bala Dhamam Hemashailabha Deham
Danujvana Krishanum Jnaneenam Agraganyam
Sakala Guna Nidhanam Vanaranam Adhisham
Raghu Pati Priya Bhaktam Vatajatam Namami
content.meaning: I bow to the son of the wind god, whose strength is immeasurable, whose body shines like a golden mountain, who is like fire to the forest of demons, who is foremost among the wise, who is a treasure of all virtues, who is the chief of the vanaras, and who is the beloved devotee of Lord Rama.
content.transliteration:
Atul Bala Dhāmaṁ Hemaśailābha Dehaṁ
Danujvana Kṛśānuṁ Jñānīnāṁ Agragaṇyam
Sakala Guṇa Nidhānaṁ Vānarāṇāṁ Adhīśaṁ
Raghu Pati Priya Bhaktaṁ Vātajātaṁ Namāmi

content.shloka:
Om Namo Hanumate Bhaybhanjanaya
Sukham Kuru Phat Svaha
Om Namo Hanumate Rudravataraya
Sarva Shtroon Samharakaraaya
Sarvavyadhi Nivarakaya Svaha
content.meaning: Om, salutations to Hanuman, destroyer of fear, grant me happiness. Om, salutations to Hanuman, the incarnation of Rudra, the destroyer of all enemies, the remover of all diseases, Svaha.
content.transliteration:
Om Namo Hanumate Bhaybhañjanāya
Sukhaṁ Kuru Phaṭ Svāhā
Om Namo Hanumate Rudrāvatārāya
Sarva Śatrūn Saṁhārakārāya
Sarvavyādhi Nivārakāya Svāhā

content.shloka:
Om Sahana Vavatu
Saha Nau Bhunaktu
Saha Viryam Karavavahai
Tejasvinavadhitamastu
Ma Vidvishavahai
Om Shantih Shantih Shantih
content.meaning: May the Lord protect us both (teacher and student). May He nourish us both. May we work together with great energy. May our study be enlightening and fruitful. May we never have hostility towards each other. Om, peace, peace, peace.
content.transliteration:
Om Saha Nāvavatu
Saha Nau Bhunaktu
Saha Vīryaṁ Karavāvahai
Tejasvi Nāvadhītamastu
Mā Vidviṣāvahai
Om Śāntiḥ Śāntiḥ Śāntiḥ

content.shloka:
Om Asato Ma Sadgamaya
Tamaso Ma Jyotirgamaya
Mrityor Ma Amritam Gamaya
Om Shantih Shantih Shantih
content.meaning: Lead me from the unreal to the real. Lead me from darkness to light. Lead me from death to immortality. Om, peace, peace, peace. This is from the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.
content.transliteration:
Om Asato Mā Sadgamaya
Tamaso Mā Jyotirgamaya
Mṛtyor Mā Amṛtaṁ Gamaya
Om Śāntiḥ Śāntiḥ Śāntiḥ

content.shloka:
Om Purnamadah Purnamidam
Purnat Purnamudachyate
Purnasya Purnamadaya
Purnamevavashishyate
Om Shantih Shantih Shantih
content.meaning: That (Brahman) is whole. This (universe) is whole. From the whole, the whole arises. When the whole is taken from the whole, the whole still remains. Om, peace, peace, peace. This is the Isha Upanishad invocation.
content.transliteration:
Om Pūrṇamadaḥ Pūrṇamidaṁ
Pūrṇāt Pūrṇamudachyate
Pūrṇasya Pūrṇamādāya
Pūrṇamevāvaśiṣyate
Om Śāntiḥ Śāntiḥ Śāntiḥ

content.shloka:
Om Sarve Bhavantu Sukhinah
Sarve Santu Niramayah
Sarve Bhadrani Pashyantu
Ma Kashchid Duhkha Bhag Bhavet
Om Shantih Shantih Shantih
content.meaning: May all beings be happy. May all beings be free from illness. May all beings see what is auspicious. May no one suffer. Om, peace, peace, peace. This universal prayer expresses the highest ideal of Vedic spirituality.
content.transliteration:
Om Sarve Bhavantu Sukhinaḥ
Sarve Santu Nirāmayāḥ
Sarve Bhadrāṇi Paśyantu
Mā Kaśchid Duḥkha Bhāg Bhavet
Om Śāntiḥ Śāntiḥ Śāntiḥ

content.shloka:
Om Dyauh Shantih Antariksha Shantih
Prithvi Shantih Apah Shantih
Oshadhayah Shantih
Vanaspatayah Shantih
Vishvedevah Shantih
Brahma Shantih
Sarvam Shantih Shantirev Shantih
Sa Ma Shantiredhi
Om Shantih Shantih Shantih
content.meaning: May there be peace in the heavens, peace in the atmosphere, peace on earth, peace in water, peace in plants, peace in trees, peace in all the gods, peace in Brahman, peace in everything. May that peace, real peace, be mine. Om, peace, peace, peace.
content.transliteration:
Om Dyauḥ Śāntiḥ Antarikṣa Śāntiḥ
Pṛthvī Śāntiḥ Āpaḥ Śāntiḥ
Oṣadhayaḥ Śāntiḥ
Vanaspatayaḥ Śāntiḥ
Viśvedevāḥ Śāntiḥ
Brahma Śāntiḥ
Sarvaṁ Śāntiḥ Śāntireva Śāntiḥ
Sā Mā Śāntiredhi
Om Śāntiḥ Śāntiḥ Śāntiḥ

content.shloka:
Om Suryaya Namah
Japa Kusuma Sankasham
Kashyapeyam Mahadyutim
Tamo Arim Sarva Papghnam
Pranato Asmi Divaakaram
content.meaning: Salutations to Surya (Sun). I bow to the one who is radiant like the Japa flower (hibiscus), who is the son of Kashyapa, who possesses great brilliance, who is the enemy of darkness and destroyer of all sins. I prostrate before the Lord of the Day.
content.transliteration:
Om Sūryāya Namaḥ
Japā Kusuma Saṅkāśaṁ
Kāśyapeyaṁ Mahādyutim
Tamo Ariṁ Sarva Pāpaghnaṁ
Praṇato Asmi Divākaram

content.shloka:
Om Chandraya Namah
Dadhi Shankha Tushaarabham
Kshirodarnava Sambhavam
Namami Shashinam Somam
Shambhor Makuta Bhushanam
content.meaning: Salutations to Chandra (Moon). I bow to the Moon who is as white as yogurt, conch shell, and frost, who emerged from the ocean of milk, who is adorned with moonbeams, and who is the ornament on Lord Shambhu's (Shiva's) crown.
content.transliteration:
Om Chandrāya Namaḥ
Dadhi Śaṅkha Tuṣārābhaṁ
Kṣīrodārnava Sambhavam
Namāmi Śaśinaṁ Somaṁ
Śambhor Makuṭa Bhūṣaṇam

content.shloka:
Om Mangalaya Namah
Dharaniigarbha Sambhutam
Vidyut Kanti Samaprabham
Kumaram Shakti Hastam Cha
Mangalam Pranamamy Aham
content.meaning: Salutations to Mangala (Mars). I bow to Mars who is born from the womb of the Earth, who shines with the radiance of lightning, who is youthful, who holds the Shakti weapon in his hand. I prostrate before the auspicious one.
content.transliteration:
Om Maṅgalāya Namaḥ
Dharaṇīgarbha Sambhūtaṁ
Vidyut Kānti Samaprabhām
Kumāraṁ Śakti Hastaṁ Cha
Maṅgalaṁ Praṇamāmyaham

content.shloka:
Om Budhaya Namah
Priyangukalika Shyamam
Rupenaa Pratimam Budham
Saumyam Saumya Gunopetam
Tam Budham Pranamamy Aham
content.meaning: Salutations to Budha (Mercury). I bow to Mercury who is dark like the bud of the priyangu plant, whose beauty is unequaled, who is gentle and endowed with gentle qualities. I prostrate before Budha.
content.transliteration:
Om Budhāya Namaḥ
Priyaṅgukalikā Śyāmaṁ
Rūpeṇā Pratimaṁ Budham
Saumyaṁ Saumya Guṇopetaṁ
Taṁ Budhaṁ Praṇamāmyaham

content.shloka:
Om Gurave Namah
Devanaam Cha Rishinaam Cha
Gurum Kaanchana Sannibham
Buddhi Bhutam Trilokesham
Tam Namami Brihaspatim
content.meaning: Salutations to Guru (Jupiter/Brihaspati). I bow to the Guru of gods and sages, who shines like gold, who is the embodiment of wisdom, and who is the lord of the three worlds. I prostrate before Brihaspati.
content.transliteration:
Om Gurave Namaḥ
Devānāṁ Cha Ṛṣīṇāṁ Cha
Guruṁ Kāñchana Sannibham
Buddhi Bhūtaṁ Trilokeśaṁ
Taṁ Namāmi Bṛhaspatim

content.shloka:
Om Shukraya Namah
Hima Kunda Mrinalabham
Daityanam Paramam Gurum
Sarva Shastra Pravaktaram
Bhargavam Pranamamy Aham
content.meaning: Salutations to Shukra (Venus). I bow to the one who is as white as snow, jasmine, and lotus stem, who is the supreme guru of the demons, who is the expounder of all scriptures. I prostrate before Bhargava (Shukracharya).
content.transliteration:
Om Śukrāya Namaḥ
Hima Kunda Mṛṇālābhaṁ
Daityānāṁ Paramaṁ Guruṁ
Sarva Śāstra Pravaktāraṁ
Bhārgavaṁ Praṇamāmyaham

content.shloka:
Om Shanaischaraya Namah
Nilanjana Samabhasam
Ravi Putram Yamagrajam
Chhaya Martanda Sambhutam
Tam Namami Shanaischaraam
content.meaning: Salutations to Shani (Saturn). I bow to the one who is dark as collyrium, who is the son of Surya (Sun), who is the elder brother of Yama (Lord of Death), who is born of Chhaya and the Sun. I prostrate before Shani, the slow-moving one.
content.transliteration:
Om Śanaiścharāya Namaḥ
Nīlāñjana Samābhāsaṁ
Ravi Putraṁ Yamāgrajaṁ
Chāyā Mārtaṇḍa Sambhūtaṁ
Taṁ Namāmi Śanaiścharām

content.shloka:
Om Rahave Namah
Ardha Kayam Mahaveeryam
Chandraditya Vimardanam
Simhika Garbha Sambhutam
Tam Rahum Pranamamy Aham
content.meaning: Salutations to Rahu (North Lunar Node). I bow to the one who has half a body, who possesses great valor, who oppresses the Sun and Moon (causing eclipses), who is born from the womb of Simhika. I prostrate before Rahu.
content.transliteration:
Om Rāhave Namaḥ
Ardha Kāyaṁ Mahāvīryaṁ
Candrāditya Vimardanaṁ
Siṁhikā Garbha Sambhūtaṁ
Taṁ Rāhuṁ Praṇamāmyaham

content.shloka:
Om Ketave Namah
Palaasha Pushpa Sankaasham
Taraka Graha Mastakam
Raudram Raudratmakam Ghoram
Tam Ketum Pranamamy Aham
content.meaning: Salutations to Ketu (South Lunar Node). I bow to the one who is like the palasha flower in appearance, who is the head among the stellar planets, who is fierce and terrifying in nature. I prostrate before Ketu.
content.transliteration:
Om Ketave Namaḥ
Palāśa Puṣpa Saṅkāśaṁ
Tārakā Graha Mastakam
Raudraṁ Raudrātmakaṁ Ghoraṁ
Taṁ Ketuṁ Praṇamāmyaham

content.shloka: Om Namah Shivaya
content.meaning: Salutations to Lord Shiva. This five-syllable mantra (Na-Mah-Shi-Va-Ya) is the most sacred mantra in Shaivism. The five syllables represent the five elements: Na (earth), Mah (water), Shi (fire), Va (air), Ya (space). It is the path to liberation and union with Shiva.
content.transliteration: Om Namaḥ Śivāya

content.shloka:
Nagendraharaya Trilochanaya
Bhasmangaragaya Maheshvaraya
Nityaya Shuddhaya Digambaraya
Tasmai Nakaraya Namah Shivaya
content.meaning: Salutations to the one represented by the syllable 'Na' - Lord Shiva, who wears the king of serpents as a garland, who has three eyes, whose body is smeared with sacred ash, who is the Great Lord, who is eternal, pure, and who is clad in the directions (sky-clad).
content.transliteration:
Nāgendrahārāya Trilochanāya
Bhasmāṅgarāgāya Maheśvarāya
Nityāya Śuddhāya Digambarāya
Tasmai Nakārāya Namaḥ Śivāya

content.shloka:
Mandakini Salilachandana Charchitaya
Nandiishvara Pramatha Natha Maheshvaraya
Mandarapushpa Bahupushpa Supujitaya
Tasmai Makaraya Namah Shivaya
content.meaning: Salutations to the one represented by the syllable 'Ma' - Lord Shiva, who is anointed with the water of the Ganges and sandalwood paste, who is the lord of Nandi and the Pramatha ganas, the Great Lord, who is beautifully worshipped with mandara and many other flowers.
content.transliteration:
Mandākinī Salilachandana Charchitāya
Nandīśvara Pramatha Nātha Maheśvarāya
Mandārapuṣpa Bahupuṣpa Supūjitāya
Tasmai Makārāya Namaḥ Śivāya

content.shloka:
Shivaya Gauri Vadanabja Brinda
Suryaya Dakshadhvara Nashakaya
Shri Nilakanthaya Vrisha Dhvajaya
Tasmai Shikaraya Namah Shivaya
content.meaning: Salutations to the one represented by the syllable 'Shi' - Lord Shiva, who is the sun that causes the lotus face of Gauri (Parvati) to bloom, who destroyed the sacrifice of Daksha, who has a blue throat (Nilakantha), and whose banner bears the bull.
content.transliteration:
Śivāya Gaurī Vadanābja Bṛnda
Sūryāya Dakṣādhvara Nāśakāya
Śrī Nīlakaṇṭhāya Vṛṣa Dhvajāya
Tasmai Śikārāya Namaḥ Śivāya

content.shloka:
Vasishtha Kumbhodbhava Gautamarya
Munindra Devarchita Shekharaya
Chandrarka Vaishvanara Lochanaya
Tasmai Vakaraya Namah Shivaya
content.meaning: Salutations to the one represented by the syllable 'Va' - Lord Shiva, who is worshipped by sages Vasishtha, Agastya, Gautama, and other great sages and gods, whose crown is adorned by them, and whose three eyes are the Moon, Sun, and Fire.
content.transliteration:
Vasiṣṭha Kumbhodbhava Gautamārya
Munīndra Devārchita Śekharāya
Chandrārka Vaiśvānara Lochanāya
Tasmai Vakārāya Namaḥ Śivāya

content.shloka:
Yagna Svarupaya Jataadharaya
Pinaka Hastaya Sanatanaya
Divyaya Devaya Digambaraya
Tasmai Yakaraya Namah Shivaya
content.meaning: Salutations to the one represented by the syllable 'Ya' - Lord Shiva, who is the embodiment of sacrifice (yagna), who bears matted locks, who holds the Pinaka bow in his hand, who is eternal, divine, a great god, and sky-clad.
content.transliteration:
Yajña Svarūpāya Jaṭādharāya
Pināka Hastāya Sanātanāya
Divyāya Devāya Digambarāya
Tasmai Yakārāya Namaḥ Śivāya

content.shloka: Om Namo Narayanaya
content.meaning: This is the Ashtakshara (eight-syllable) Mantra - the most sacred mantra in Vaishnavism. The eight syllables are Om-Na-Mo-Na-Ra-Ya-Na-Ya. It signifies total surrender to Lord Narayana, the supreme refuge of all beings, the one who pervades all of creation.
content.transliteration: Om Namo Nārāyaṇāya

content.shloka:
Narayanam Padmabhuvam Vashishtham
Shaktim Cha Tatputra Parasharamcha
Vyasam Shukam Gaudapadam Mahantam
Govinda Yogindra Mathasya Shishyam
content.meaning: I salute Narayana, Padmabhuva (Brahma), Vasishtha, Shakti, and his son Parashara, Vyasa, Shuka, the great Gaudapada, and his disciple, the supreme yogi Govinda. This is the Guru Parampara (lineage) invocation of the Ashtakshara tradition.
content.transliteration:
Nārāyaṇaṁ Padmabhuvaṁ Vasiṣṭhaṁ
Śaktiṁ Cha Tatputra Parāśaraṁcha
Vyāsaṁ Śukaṁ Gauḍapadaṁ Mahāntaṁ
Govinda Yogīndra Mathāsya Śiṣyam

content.shloka:
Om Namo Narayanaya Ashtakshara
Maha Mantrena Sarva Papaat
Pramuchyate Iti Vaidikamanah
content.meaning: By the great eight-syllable mantra 'Om Namo Narayanaya,' one is freed from all sins. This is the declaration of the Vedic tradition. The mantra is considered the essence of all Vedic teachings and the direct path to moksha (liberation).
content.transliteration:
Om Namo Nārāyaṇāya Aṣṭākṣara
Mahā Mantreṇa Sarva Pāpāt
Pramuchyate Iti Vaidikamanāḥ

content.shloka:
Narayana Para Jyotih
Atma Narayanah Parah
Narayana Param Brahma
Narayana Namostute
content.meaning: Narayana is the supreme light. Narayana is the supreme Self. Narayana is the supreme Brahman. Salutations to Lord Narayana. He is the ultimate reality beyond all manifestation.
content.transliteration:
Nārāyaṇa Parā Jyotiḥ
Ātmā Nārāyaṇaḥ Paraḥ
Nārāyaṇa Paraṁ Brahma
Nārāyaṇa Namostute

content.shloka:
Namo Narayana Vidmahe
Vasudevaya Dhimahi
Tanno Vishnuh Prachodayat
content.meaning: We know Narayana, we meditate upon Vasudeva. May Lord Vishnu illuminate and inspire our intellect. This is the Narayana Gayatri, recited as part of the Ashtakshara sadhana to deepen one's connection with the Supreme.
content.transliteration:
Namo Nārāyaṇa Vidmahe
Vāsudevāya Dhīmahi
Tanno Viṣṇuḥ Prachodayāt

content.shloka:
Ksheera Sagara Shayanam
Bhujanga Shayana Uttamam
Padmanabham Suresham Cha
Narayanam Aham Bhaje
content.meaning: I worship Lord Narayana, who reclines on the ocean of milk, who rests upon the supreme serpent Shesha, from whose navel the lotus emerges, and who is the lord of all the gods.
content.transliteration:
Kṣīra Sāgara Śayanaṁ
Bhujanga Śayana Uttamam
Padmanābhaṁ Sureśaṁ Cha
Nārāyaṇaṁ Ahaṁ Bhaje

content.shloka:
Om Namo Bhagavate
Vasudevaya Dhanvantaraye
Amrita Kalasha Hastaya
Sarva Amaya Vinashanaya
Trilokanathaya
Shri Mahavishnave Namah
content.meaning: Salutations to the Supreme Lord Vasudeva, in the form of Dhanvantari, who holds the vessel of nectar (amrita) in his hands, who destroys all diseases, who is the lord of the three worlds, and who is the great Lord Vishnu.
content.transliteration:
Om Namo Bhagavate
Vāsudevāya Dhanvantaraye
Amṛta Kalaśa Hastāya
Sarva Āmaya Vināśanāya
Trilokanāthāya
Śrī Mahāviṣṇave Namaḥ

content.shloka: Om Dham Dhanvantaraye Namah
content.meaning: Salutations to Lord Dhanvantari. 'Dham' is the beeja (seed) mantra of Dhanvantari. This simple yet powerful mantra is chanted for healing and good health. Dhanvantari is the divine physician and the originator of Ayurveda.
content.transliteration: Om Dhaṁ Dhanvantaraye Namaḥ

content.shloka:
Om Shankham Chakram Jalaukam Cha
Dadhad Amrita Bhaajanam
Chatur Bhujam Sukha Sthanam
Dhanvantarim Namamy Aham
content.meaning: I bow to Lord Dhanvantari, who holds a conch, discus, leech, and a pot of divine nectar in his four hands, and who is the abode of happiness and well-being.
content.transliteration:
Om Śaṅkhaṁ Chakraṁ Jalaukāṁ Cha
Dadhad Amṛta Bhājanam
Chatur Bhujaṁ Sukha Sthānaṁ
Dhanvantariṁ Namāmyaham

content.shloka:
Achyutananda Govinda
Namochante Narasimha
Rogaan Me Nashaya Asheshan
Ashunaam Iva Marutah
content.meaning: O Achyuta (the infallible), O Ananda (bliss), O Govinda, O Narasimha, I bow to you. Destroy all my diseases completely, just as the wind sweeps away all things in its path.
content.transliteration:
Achyutānanda Govinda
Namochante Narasiṁha
Rogān Me Nāśaya Aśeṣān
Āśunāṁ Iva Mārutaḥ

content.shloka:
Dhanvantari Dhyana Shloka:
Neelambhoja Shyamala Komala Angam
Prasanna Vaktram Nalinayataksham
Samasta Roga Prashama Pranasham
Dhanvantarim Loka Hitam Namami
content.meaning: Dhanvantari Meditation Verse: I bow to Lord Dhanvantari, whose body is soft and dark like a blue lotus, whose face is serene, whose eyes are long like lotus petals, who alleviates all diseases, and who is devoted to the welfare of all the worlds.
content.transliteration:
Dhanvantari Dhyāna Śloka:
Nīlāmbhoja Śyāmala Komala Aṅgaṁ
Prasanna Vaktraṁ Nalināyatākṣam
Samasta Roga Praśama Praṇāśaṁ
Dhanvantariṁ Loka Hitaṁ Namāmi

content.shloka:
Om Shreem Hreem Kleem Glaum
Devakisuta Govinda
Vaasudeva Jagatpate
Dehime Tanayam Krishna
Tvaamaham Sharanam Gatah
content.meaning: Om, with the sacred seed syllables Shreem, Hreem, Kleem, and Glaum - O son of Devaki, O Govinda, O Vasudeva, O Lord of the Universe, O Krishna, please bless me with a child. I have taken refuge in you.
content.transliteration:
Om Śrīṁ Hrīṁ Klīṁ Glauṁ
Devakīsuta Govinda
Vāsudeva Jagatpate
Dehime Tanayaṁ Kṛṣṇa
Tvāmahaṁ Śaraṇaṁ Gataḥ

content.shloka:
Om Kleem Gopalveshdharine
Vasudevaya Hooh Phat Svaha
content.meaning: Om, I invoke Lord Vasudeva who is adorned in the form of a cowherd boy (Gopala). This is the beeja mantra form of the Santan Gopal Mantra. It is chanted for the blessing of progeny and protection of children.
content.transliteration:
Om Klīṁ Gopālavesdhāriṇe
Vāsudevāya Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā

content.shloka:
Shloka Dhyanam:
Vasudeva Sutam Devam
Kamsa Chanura Mardanam
Devaki Paramanandam
Krishnam Vande Jagadgurum
content.meaning: Meditation Verse: I worship Lord Krishna, the son of Vasudeva, the destroyer of Kamsa and Chanura, the supreme bliss of Devaki, and the spiritual teacher of the entire universe.
content.transliteration:
Śloka Dhyānam:
Vasudeva Sutaṁ Devaṁ
Kaṁsa Chāṇūra Mardanam
Devakī Paramānandaṁ
Kṛṣṇaṁ Vande Jagadgurum

content.shloka:
Krishna Krishna Mahayogin
Bhaktanam Abhayankara
Govinda Paramananda
Sarvam Me Vasha Manaya
content.meaning: O Krishna, O great Yogi, O protector who removes the fear of devotees, O Govinda, O Supreme Bliss, bring everything under my benevolent control and bless me with fulfillment.
content.transliteration:
Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Mahāyogin
Bhaktānāṁ Abhayaṅkara
Govinda Paramānanda
Sarvaṁ Me Vaśa Mānaya

content.shloka:
Phalashruti:
Santan Gopal Mantrasya
Japena Putra Labhanam
Sarva Kama Pradayinam
Sarva Saubhagya Dayakam
content.meaning: Fruit of Recitation: By the chanting of the Santan Gopal Mantra, one obtains the blessing of children. This mantra fulfills all desires and bestows all kinds of good fortune and auspiciousness.
content.transliteration:
Phalaśruti:
Santān Gopāl Mantrasya
Japena Putra Lābhanaṁ
Sarva Kāma Pradāyinaṁ
Sarva Saubhāgya Dāyakam

content.shloka:
Gurur Brahma Gurur Vishnu
Gurur Devo Maheshvarah
Guruh Sakshat Parabrahma
Tasmai Shri Gurave Namah
content.meaning: The Guru is Brahma (the Creator), the Guru is Vishnu (the Preserver), the Guru is Lord Maheshvara (Shiva, the Destroyer). The Guru is verily the Supreme Brahman itself. Salutations to that glorious Guru.
content.transliteration:
Gurur Brahmā Gurur Viṣṇuḥ
Gurur Devo Maheśvaraḥ
Guruḥ Sākṣāt Parabrahma
Tasmai Śrī Gurave Namaḥ

content.shloka:
Akhanda Mandalakaram
Vyaptam Yena Characharam
Tatpadam Darshitam Yena
Tasmai Shri Gurave Namah
content.meaning: Salutations to the Guru who has revealed that state which pervades the entire unbroken form of the universe, comprising both the moving and the unmoving. The Guru shows us the truth of existence that permeates all things.
content.transliteration:
Akhaṇḍa Maṇḍalākāraṁ
Vyāptaṁ Yena Charācharam
Tatpadaṁ Darśitaṁ Yena
Tasmai Śrī Gurave Namaḥ

content.shloka:
Ajnana Timirandhasya
Jnananjana Shalakaya
Chakshur Unmilitam Yena
Tasmai Shri Gurave Namah
content.meaning: Salutations to the Guru who, with the collyrium stick of knowledge, has opened the eyes of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance. The Guru is the remover of spiritual darkness.
content.transliteration:
Ajñāna Timirāndhasya
Jñānāñjana Śalākayā
Chakṣur Unmīlitaṁ Yena
Tasmai Śrī Gurave Namaḥ

content.shloka:
Dhyana Mulam Guror Murtih
Puja Mulam Guroh Padam
Mantra Mulam Guror Vakyam
Moksha Mulam Guroh Kripa
content.meaning: The root of meditation is the Guru's form. The root of worship is the Guru's feet. The root of mantra is the Guru's word. The root of liberation is the Guru's grace. All spiritual practice originates from the Guru.
content.transliteration:
Dhyāna Mūlaṁ Guror Mūrtiḥ
Pūjā Mūlaṁ Guroḥ Padam
Mantra Mūlaṁ Guror Vākyaṁ
Mokṣa Mūlaṁ Guroḥ Kṛpā

content.shloka:
Brahmanandam Parama Sukhadam
Kevalam Jnana Murtim
Dvandvatitam Gagana Sadrisham
Tattvamasyadi Lakshyam
Ekam Nityam Vimalam Achalam
Sarvadhee Sakshi Bhutam
Bhavatitam Triguna Rahitam
Sadgurum Tam Namami
content.meaning: I salute the true Guru who is the bliss of Brahman, who bestows supreme happiness, who is the embodiment of pure knowledge, who transcends all dualities, who is vast as the sky, who is the goal of the great Vedic statement 'Thou art That,' who is one, eternal, pure, immovable, the witness of all intellects, who is beyond worldly existence and free from the three qualities (gunas).
content.transliteration:
Brahmānandaṁ Parama Sukhadaṁ
Kevalaṁ Jñāna Mūrtim
Dvandvātītaṁ Gagana Sadṛśaṁ
Tattvamasyādi Lakṣyam
Ekaṁ Nityaṁ Vimalaṁ Achalaṁ
Sarvadhī Sākṣi Bhūtam
Bhāvātītaṁ Triguṇa Rahitaṁ
Sadguruṁ Taṁ Namāmi

content.shloka:
Guru Gita Sara:
Gurureva Jagat Sarvam
Brahma Vishnu Shivamakam
Guroh Parataram Nasti
Tasmat Sampujayed Gurum
content.meaning: Essence of Guru Gita: The Guru is the entire universe, the Guru is Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva combined. There is nothing higher than the Guru. Therefore, one should worship the Guru with utmost devotion.
content.transliteration:
Guru Gītā Sāra:
Gurureva Jagat Sarvaṁ
Brahmā Viṣṇu Śivātmakam
Guroḥ Parataraṁ Nāsti
Tasmāt Sampūjayed Gurum
